newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICAN CHIEF RESIGNS AFTER DAMNING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUTH AFRICAN CHIEF RESIGNS AFTER DAMNING REPORT.

text.p: South African Football Association executive president Solomon Morewa resigned on Wednesday after a damning report described him as unfit to run soccer in the country.
Morewa, 54, announced his resignation eight days after the release of a judical commission into the running of South African soccer, which recommended he stepped down.

"I don't want to be the source of division in South African soccer," he said while announcing his resignation after returning from Lisbon where he collected a FIFA award on behalf of South Africa as the most improved side of 1996.
"A lot of people have a lot of different opinions on whether I should stay or go and I worked very hard for unity in South African soccer that I don't want to split it now," he said.
Morewa was heavily criticised in the 102-page report by Justice Benjamin Poickard, who was mandated in May by sports minister Steve Tshwete to investigate possible corruption in South African soccer.

The investigation found Morewa had received a loan of 500,000 rand ($107,000) from a marketing company granted the rights to organise international matches for the South African national team and a Mercedes Benz car from a tournament sponsor.

He was also found to have awarded himself a study bursary from a football association fund specifically designed to finance players' education and bonus payments following South Africa's win in last year's African Nations Cup.
The commission said: "He has proven himself to be over concerned with promoting his own interests instead of those of his association and should resign."
Last week Morewa said he would wait until a special general meeting of the association on February 9 decided his fate.
But on Wednesday he said he had changed his mind after "a lot of soul searching".
"I still don't agree with the report," said Morewa, who pointed out he had not been accused of doing anything illegal.
Morewa told radio interviewers he had not discussed the matter with FIFA at its annual award ceremony in Lisbon on Monday.
But a FIFA press release from Zurich said he had a meeting on the issue with FIFA president Joao Havelange and secretary-general Sepp Blatter.
